bib.title: Weight Normalization: A Simple Reparameterization to Accelerate Training of Deep Neural Networks

question: Can reparameterizing each weight vector into a scale and a direction speed up SGD convergence, with less cost and noise than batch normalization?
hypothesis: Decoupling weight-vector length from direction improves the conditioning of the optimization problem and speeds up convergence, giving much of the benefit of batch normalization without minibatch dependence.
contributions: Weight normalization: w = (g/||v||) v, SGD on v and g
Data-dependent initialization of g and b from one minibatch
Mean-only batch normalization, combined with weight normalization
Experiments on CIFAR-10 classification, convolutional VAE, DRAW and DQN

method.summary: Each neuron weight vector w is reparameterized as w = g v/||v||, and SGD runs on v and g. g and b are initialized from one minibatch so pre-activations have zero mean and unit variance. Tested on four models: CIFAR-10 CNN, convolutional VAE (MNIST, CIFAR-10), DRAW (MNIST) and DQN (Atari).
method.task: supervised image classification, generative modelling, deep reinforcement learning

datasets.name: CIFAR-10
datasets.split: 10000 examples held out to tune the Gaussian noise std; test set reported

datasets.name: Atari Learning Environment (Breakout, Enduro, Seaquest, Space Invaders)
datasets.preprocessing: follows Mnih et al. as closely as possible

models.name: CIFAR-10 CNN (ConvPool-CNN-C variant)
models.architecture: conv net, 3x3 convs with leaky ReLU, 96 then 192 channels, global average pool, softmax

other.changes_from_ConvPool-CNN-C: first dropout layer replaced by Gaussian noise (sigma 0.15 in Table 1), last hidden layer expanded from 10 to 192 units, 2x2 max-pool instead of 3x3

models.name: Convolutional VAE with ResNet blocks
models.architecture: MNIST encoder: 3 sequences of two ResNet blocks (16, 32, 32 feature maps), 2x subsampling by 2x2 stride after first two, then fully connected layer with 450 units; decoder mirrors; auto-regressive variational inference; CIFAR-10 version has multiple intermediate stochastic layers (details deferred to manuscript in preparation)

models.name: DRAW
models.architecture: VAE with LSTM encoder and decoder; weight normalization applied to all weight vectors

models.name: DQN
models.architecture: Deep Q-Network of Mnih et al. 2015, Python/Theano/Lasagne reimplementation

training.objective: CIFAR-10: classification error; VAE and DRAW: lower bound on marginal likelihood; DQN: Q-learning
training.optimizer: CIFAR-10: Adam, momentum 0.9 for first 100 epochs then 0.5; VAE: Adamax; DQN: Adamax with momentum 0.5
training.lr: CIFAR-10: best of {0.0003, 0.001, 0.003, 0.01} (Fig 1: 0.003 for WN/BN/mean-only BN, 0.0003 for normal); VAE: alpha=0.002; DQN: best of {0.0001, 0.0003, 0.001, 0.003}, 0.0003 with WN, 0.0001 normal
training.lr_schedule: CIFAR-10: fixed for first 100 epochs, linearly decayed to zero over last 100
training.epochs: CIFAR-10: 200; VAE MNIST plotted to ~300 and CIFAR-10 to ~450; DRAW: 100 (not converged); DQN: 200 plotted
training.regularisation: Gaussian input noise sigma=0.15 (CIFAR-10); Polyak averaging as exponential moving average over about 10 epochs (VAE)
training.hardware: DQN: Amazon EC2 g2.2xlarge GPU instance
training.seeds: VAE MNIST: multiple random seeds (number not given), standard error bars

other.init: v ~ Normal(0, 0.05); g and b set from one minibatch: g=1/sigma[t], b=-mu[t]/sigma[t]
other.log_scale_g: g=e^s tried; test performance not significantly different, optimization slightly slower
other.noise_std_tuning: only hyperparameter actively tuned, on 10000 holdout, with standard parameterization

other.mean_only_BN_test_time: running average of minibatch mean substituted at test time

metrics.name: CIFAR-10 test error
metrics.definition: classification error on the test set

metrics.name: marginal likelihood lower bound
metrics.definition: test-set bound for VAE and DRAW

baselines: published CIFAR-10 nets: Maxout, Network in Network, Deeply Supervised, ConvPool-CNN-C, ALL-CNN-C
eval.protocol: CIFAR-10: single run per parameterization, best learning rate chosen from grid; VAE MNIST has seed error bars; others single curves. No significance tests.

evidence.quote: For each case we pick the optimal learning rate in {0.0003, 0.001, 0.003, 0.01}.

results.claim: Weight norm plus mean-only batch norm gives the lowest CIFAR-10 test error, 7.31%, claimed state of the art without augmentation.
results.setup: CIFAR-10 test set, no data augmentation, ConvPool-CNN-C-based CNN, Adam, 200 epochs, batch 100, best lr in {0.0003,0.001,0.003,0.01}
results.quote: has the best performance at 7.31% test error

results.claim: Full batch norm reaches 8.05% test error on CIFAR-10.
results.setup: CIFAR-10 test set, no data augmentation, ConvPool-CNN-C-based CNN, Adam, 200 epochs, batch 100, best lr in {0.0003,0.001,0.003,0.01}
results.table: Fig 2 (Table 2), row our CNN, batch norm.

results.claim: Weight norm alone gives 8.46% test error, about the same as the normal parameterization (8.43%).
results.setup: CIFAR-10 test set, no data augmentation, ConvPool-CNN-C-based CNN, Adam, 200 epochs, batch 100, best lr in {0.0003,0.001,0.003,0.01}
results.table: Fig 2 (Table 2), row our CNN, weight norm.

results.claim: Mean-only batch norm with the normal parameterization gives 8.52% test error.
results.setup: CIFAR-10 test set, no data augmentation, ConvPool-CNN-C-based CNN, Adam, 200 epochs, batch 100, best lr in {0.0003,0.001,0.003,0.01}
results.table: Fig 2 (Table 2), row our CNN, mean-only B.N.

results.claim: Batch norm training was about 16% slower than the standard parameterization; weight norm was not noticeably slower.
results.quote: was about 16% slower compared to the standard parameterization

results.claim: Weight norm and batch norm both speed up CIFAR-10 training error reduction versus the normal parameterization (Fig 1), batch norm slightly faster per epoch early on.
results.setup: CIFAR-10, Adam lr 0.003 for WN/BN, 0.0003 normal

results.claim: DQN Space Invaders max score is 2,179 with weight norm versus 1,779 normal and 1,975 for Mnih et al.
results.setup: DQN, Adamax, batch 64, lr 0.0003 WN / 0.0001 normal
results.table: Figure 6, row Space Invaders, column weightnorm

results.claim: DQN Enduro max score is 1,448 with weight norm versus 1,250 normal and 302 for Mnih et al.
results.note: authors suggest the gap to Mnih may be due to no play-time limit

results.claim: DQN Breakout: 403 with weight norm versus 410 normal (no gain).
DQN Seaquest: 7,375 with weight norm versus 7,188 normal.
Batch norm could not be made to work for DQN without an impractically large minibatch; weight norm worked.
results.quote: We were not able to get batch normalization to work for DQN without using an impractically large minibatch size.

results.claim: Weight norm gives lower variance and a better optimum for the convolutional VAE on MNIST and CIFAR-10 (read from Fig 3, no number given).
results.setup: Convolutional VAE, Adamax alpha 0.002, seed error bars on MNIST

results.claim: Weight norm speeds up DRAW convergence on MNIST without retuning init or learning rate; 100 epochs not enough for convergence.
Weight norm makes training robust to the learning rate because the norm of v grows until the effective rate is suitable.
results.setup: Argument in section 2.1, no dedicated experiment

limits: Single run per setting on CIFAR-10, no seeds or significance tests reported
Explanations for the mean-only BN gain (kurtosis of noise) are hypotheses, not tested
Data-dependent init cannot be used for RNN/LSTM; standard init used there
Norm-growth analysis strictly holds only for plain SGD, not Adam or momentum
No ImageNet or large-scale language results; no learning-rate robustness experiment shown
CVAE CIFAR-10 architecture deferred to an unpublished manuscript
DQN comparison to Mnih confounded by reimplementation differences
